User annotation 3, 2026-10-20. Activity board headers currently mix green/gray/black across nesting, while Node editor Components and component headers share the same green. Establish reusable nesting color ownership rather than separate per-view styling.
Use a brighter green at the root and a darker green at the deepest known level. Define two stable endpoint colors; distribute intermediate levels equally across that range according to the known nesting depth. When the known depth changes, recalculate intermediate colors while keeping endpoints stable. Apply the same system to Activity board and Node editor headers, with scope for later consumers.
Refine the scope of known depth, the single-level case, interpolation/color space and accessible text contrast during implementation. Preserve the requested endpoint stability and maximize visible distinction between levels.

2026-10-24 implementation: 275de1c and c957885 share root #367a47 and deepest #17381f endpoints, white text, and equally spaced encoded-sRGB intermediate colors. Known depth includes collapsed groups; a single level uses the root color. Board and Node editor use the shared owner. Contrast checks, depth cases, exact rendered colors, and screenshots pass; Completed: focused owner/consumer checks and exact browser recordings pass, including the affected scenarios in both full browser runs. Disposable UI screenshots were inspected. The overall checkpoint follow-up is tracked separately on the native Windows worker task.

Final checkpoint, 2026-10-24, commit 6a04fdf: build and type checks passed (1,164 authored files, zero violations); all 668 non-browser tests passed. This task's affected browser scenarios passed and UI screenshots were inspected where applicable. The full browser run passed 292/294, with separate native-worker and review-acceptance failures retained as queued investigations. Both failed cases passed unchanged in isolation. Live application restarted successfully. Detailed report: .harness/overnight-verification-20261024.json.
